candidate_originals.stem: A patient presents a valid clozapine prescription in August 2026. candidate_originals.stem: A properly authorized New Hampshire practitioner telephones a lawful alprazolam prescription to a Massachusetts pharmacist. The pharmacist verifies the Schedule IV prescription under the out-of-state pathway. A staff member says the pharmacy must wait for a written prescription before dispensing. Which response is most accurate?

choices.text: Treat the call as a Schedule II emergency prescription and require the Schedule II follow-up process before any dispensing.
Use the Schedule III-V oral pathway; record a request for the practitioner's written prescription within seven days or any shorter controlling federal period.
Dispense now and wait six months before asking the practitioner for any written record.
Ask the patient to create and sign the written follow-up because the original prescription was oral.
Reject every out-of-state oral Schedule III-V prescription because Massachusetts recognizes only electronic out-of-state prescriptions.

candidate_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is working with three support personnel who satisfy the applicable supervisory ratio. A cashier who rings up front-store sales and never assists with prescriptions is also on duty. The Manager of Record asks whether the cashier pushes the pharmacist over the ratio. What is the correct analysis?

choices.text: The cashier is excluded from the ratio because they do not support the pharmacist in a professional capacity.
The cashier counts as a fourth support person and the ratio is exceeded.
The cashier counts unless the pharmacy documents a written exemption.
The cashier counts only during hours when the pharmacy department is open.
The cashier counts as half of a support person for ratio purposes.
